Tornadoes most commonly occur in the central regions of the United States, particularly in the Great Plains, the Midwest, and the Mississippi Valley [1][3][4]. These areas, often referred to as "Tornado Alley," experience the highest frequency of tornado activity due to the convergence of cold, dry air from the Canadian provinces and warm, moist air from the Gulf of Mexico [1][3][4]. Oklahoma and Kansas are among the states hit by the most tornadoes [1][3][4]. Florida, despite having the most tornadoes per unit area, experiences mostly weak tornadoes [1][3][4]. While tornadoes can occur in any U.S. state, they are relatively rare west of the Rocky Mountains [1].
